chapters.title: the art of slow living
chapters.html:
Okhema was always a city full of surprises for Mydei.

So many of the citizens took their time in the mornings and slept late after one too many dips in their cups, and yet the days would restart again with the sounds of laughing children and scolding grandmothers. The Kremnoans had assimilated rather begrudgingly as they could, and Mydei himself enjoyed relentless praise for his war efforts and bashful smiles from naive Okheman women.

Truthfully, most of the Chrysos Heirs were struggling to find balance with the new world filled with peace instead of a constant battle against the black tide, and their regular meetings now took half the time they used to, mostly consisting of logistical concerns with the city. Even now, with mass migrations of people reinvigorating actual trade lines, the city of Okhema was still as vibrant as ever.

These thoughts melded in Mydei’s head as he walked through the market, a wooden basket cradled into the crook of his elbow. Most of his shopping these days consisted of restocks of the pantry as opposed to his former route by the smithy, but sentiment always kept him running by Chartonus even if it was off his new route. The blacksmith was wisened as ever as his hammer came down harsh on his choice of metal for the day.

“Come to my shop, you have,” Chartonus remarked, helmeted head still facing down at the bladework. “For what reason?”

Mydei huffed a quiet laugh. “Is it not enough to visit for old times sake anymore?”

At his words, the Mountain Dweller seemed to pause the swing of his hammer, opting instead to glance at Mydei. “Something on your mind, there is?”

“No,” Mydei smiled, “truly there isn’t. At least not anything serious that is.”

They exchanged a few more words from there, shortly discussing some of Chartonus’ new commissions before Mydei decided it would be better for him to continue shopping as the day passed. That was different too now, the day actually melded into night in the holy city now.

The first ‘night’ in Okhema after the black tide’s erasure was strange and uncomfortable instead of celebrated with victory. No one could be sure if it was there due to an issue with the Titans or an impending, encroaching doom hovering over the city’s core like a guillotine.

It took some time, but now that night had begun to fall upon them as usual, many vendors found themselves much more busy during the day with even more leisure in the evenings. Before they all packed up, it would be better to make quick rounds through the market, and stop to chat later.

Mydei continued his calculated wandering, saying hello to the city’s children and soldiers alike. His status as a Chrysos Heir typically made it hard for widespread affections, but the people living in the city were mostly appreciative, even with his omega status. That was the closest time he’d ever been to being nervous for a public appearance.

For most of their time fighting the black tide, Mydei asked Aglaea to keep his omega status a secret until the fighting was over, or he was permanently rid of this world. It was mainly a precaution for the Kremnoans not to be seen as weak, led by a weaker, omega prince. The woman agreed—not without issue, but her respect for his thinking about the bigger picture is what seemed to have won her over.

Once all the conflict ended though, he had no more reason to lie about his “unpresented” status. Firstly, he’d consulted with Krateros (who simply agreed quietly for the first time ever), then he confided in the detachment’s opinions. As with any society, they were mixed, but Mydei couldn’t be mad when the unwavering support of him as a warrior was still prevalent—many relieved that his prowess was something he’d also worked hard for, an achievable goal.

Surprisingly, the Okheman citizenry had taken it even better, with many omegas now proclaiming him as some sort of beating-the-odds figure. Truly, it was more complicated than that, but when he’d spoken about their response to the Goldweaver, she simply said, “I think rumors herald signs of boredom among the people, and boredom means peace.”

It was then that Mydei knew the era of war and strife had well and truly ended.

Some part of him tried not to feel lost about it all; there was no more need for the Coreflame of Strife, and Nikador, who was already widely disliked, seemed to be a thing of the past in comparison with Aquila or even Cerces. No part of him, however, was upset with the new era of peace they’d all fought for, with many people laying down their lives to defend the last bastion of hope on their planet. 

And, if peace hadn’t come—

“Mydei!”

—love wouldn’t have blossomed in its aftermath.

A sudden force propelled Mydei a few steps forward from where he stood while gathering fresh tomatoes, and arms wrapped tightly around his chest and waist. There was no give in the hold, and although Mydei could break out if he really wanted to, every part of his body seemed to relax at the scent entering his presence. Nutmeg and grapefruit flooded his senses, producing a soft giggle from Mydei as the hand not holding his basket reached up to intertwine fingers with the one wrapped around his chest.

Demetria, who’d been quite taken aback, had a warm smile on her face as she looked past him at the man who currently had his nose buried in Mydei’s neck. “Oh my, Phainon dear, please tell me you’re not here to ask for more greens than normal?”

Phainon let out a hearty laugh at her assumption as he lifted his face from scenting Mydei. “You know me too well, Lady Demetria. How about it, huh?”

Mydei rolled his eyes. “We already have so many, it’s not even remotely necessary.”

“Party pooper,” Phainon replied, smiling into a kiss placed on Mydei’s cheek.

Shortly after the black tide’s erasure was a period of rapid fire marriages and vow renewals between soldiers and their partners. Many people had declared themselves to others before going off to fight as a soldier, and now that peacetime had returned to Amphoreus, lovers were reunited and able to settle down happily with no repercussions—minus the occasional family disputes of course.

It was a busy time in the city in the months of Joy and Weaving, and at the time it came as a surprise to Mydei just how much time Phainon now spent around him. Before all of this, he’d already been liberal with his time around the Deliverer as his spirit was strong and battle prowess remarkable, but still...

Somewhere along the way though, between fighting titankin together and competing against Phainon in almost every sport or challenge known to man, Mydei found himself pondering if the joy he received from those actions was derived from somewhere deeper in his heart, somewhere more intimate.

Of course, Mydei had brushed those feelings aside at the time, but they’d lingered as heavily as a rain cloud, forever hanging over his head and heart with consequence. He’d begun to find his heats unbearable and irregular once they’d arrived, and spending them alone in his quarters around the detachment sounded more and more horrible each time. Being around Phainon so often also had the unfortunate issue of his scent being so prominent. At the time, even Phainon was unaware of his secondary gender, and the alpha pheromones he would eject during moments of battle were majorly distracting, carving their place into Mydei’s memory.

Eventually, every time Phainon would appear before him his heart would flutter and his knees would become weak. It was debilitating trying to hide the secret of his being an omega from the white haired alpha, but it was even more disarming to try and deny whatever feelings had sprung up around the man in his heart.

It wasn’t as if the feelings were unreciprocated, but Mydei hadn’t known at the time, constantly trudging through the black tide and pushing aside the growing feelings for the alpha. It wasn’t until one mission they’d taken together, where they’d gotten stuck sheltering in a cave off the shores of a forgotten city that his secret came out unintentionally.

At the time, Mydei knew his heat was due soon, but had assumed they would’ve been back to Okhema by that point. Unfortunately, the roaming titankin mixed with the beginnings of a long windstorm delayed their plans, stranding them in a cave while they waited out the trouble. Perhaps it was the close proximity to the alpha he cared for most, or maybe even a coincidence, but Mydei’s heat had started prematurely while they sheltered. 

It was a complete shock for Phainon, but even with the impossible situation, the man held his ground, speaking slowly and clearly to an uncomfortable Mydei who’d been experiencing cramping pain in pre-heat prior. “I’m here if you need me, Mydei,” he’d said, arms open. “I swear on my grave I won’t touch you in any way you don’t want.”

Mydei realized in that moment, mind addled by pheromones and stress suddenly crystal clear, that the universe paused for them. It was love, it had to be. That was why he crawled straight into those open arms at the time, maintaining physical contact with no sex on either of their minds throughout the whole thing. The scent released for him at the time had been laced with hints of adoration and affection, and some part of Mydei had begun to believe that maybe, just maybe, if things worked out regarding Amphoreus’ future, he could see himself marrying the man who held him.

Now, as their rings sparkled in the glowing daylight of the holy city, Mydei found himself laughing quietly at Phainon’s comment, continuing his tomato picking while the alpha carried on a lighthearted conversation with Demetria. He was always the better of the two when it came to intentionally appealing to the citizenry, and Mydei let him have it since their competitive streak during combat hadn’t died just yet.

Once he reached to drop coins in Demetria’s hand, she pushed his hands away, shaking her head. “A discount,” she said, pinching about half the coins in his palm for herself. “For my favorite customers.”

Phainon and Mydei exchanged glances, an expanding grin on the former’s face as Mydei thanked the woman. As soon as they’d walked off, the grin from before turned into a small laugh, the corners of his eyes crinkling from the movement. Mydei rolled his eyes again, shoving Phainon’s side with his elbow lightly. “Taking advantage of an elderly woman now? Even that isn’t beyond you, huh?”

Phainon sputtered at Mydei’s words, still giggling. “Oh come now, she called us her favorites! Don’t you think I deserve a reward for that?”

“A reward?” Mydei smiled, “What kind of reward, then?”

Phainon’s grin was in full force as he stepped in front of Mydei and began to walk backwards. “I’ll take a kiss on the cheek, or even a quick scenting!”

“I’m not scenting you right now,” Mydei scoffed.

“So you’ll kiss me instead?”

“I never said that either.”

Phainon exaggeratingly frowned, mimicking a sad chimera after a scolding. “This can’t be.”

Embarrassingly enough, Mydei’s will was not stronger than Phainon’s ability to garner pity, and after a quick speed increase, his nose bumped against Phainon’s cheek and nuzzled slightly as his lips landed there briefly, chastely giving him the kiss he so desperately wanted. Phainon’s face lit up, and he exclaimed in happiness with a fist thrown in the air from that excitement. 

Mydei huffed out a laugh while shaking his head, but the two were both smiles as they walked back together into their home, day made and evening approaching.

With all the extra time on his hands, Mydei found himself indulging in the kitchen a lot more than he used to. Many of his meals growing up consisted of sea monsters and any growing weed he could find that would make for an edible side dish. When the Kremnoan detachment moved to Okhema, his diet changed from scraps and rations to full blown meals, made right from the kitchen given to the Chrysos Heirs. At first, his shock was masked by the more pressing political issue, but as he’d settled into the city more, experimentation became a pastime for him.

The sensations while cooking were much more therapeutic than hunting and gathering for sure, yet Mydei never scorned his previous way of living too much. Even if it was unfavorable, the past was the past, and now he was happy regardless of it all.

The scent of corn permeated their cozy home as Mydei sliced the kernels off of the cob he’d gotten from shopping the day prior. Much of his cooking now considered the preservation of foods for the colder months. With the return of Aquila’s weather (now under Hyacine’s dutiful watch), the people of Amphoreus had begun to adjust to living under new kinds of uncertain conditions, and the Chrysos Heirs weren’t exempt.

Grouping his hands together around the corn, he tossed the kernels into a bowl as the creak of a door opening to his side made itself known.

“How come I always hear you before I see you?” Mydei’s cheek squished under Phainon’s kiss as the man quickly left a peck. “Have a good nap?”

“Mhm,” Phainon responded, stretching out with a yawn as he made his way to the bathroom. “Gimme a sec.”

Mydei smiled at his low energy and began packing the corn into jars, preparing them for pressure cooking. The warm water boiling on the side steamed around him as he placed the jars into the pot, lidding it just as the alpha made another appearance behind him. Arms loosely wrapped around his waist as Phainon carefully placed his head in the crook of Mydei’s neck, sniffing unabashedly at the scent of pomegranates and roselilies, sweet and yet still tart enough to offset anything sickening. 

“What are you making?” Phainon’s breath was warm against his neck and through the muffled sound, he left short kisses. “Smells good.”

“Lunch is already made, but you can help me out with this for the winter,” the omega said quietly, moving his head slightly to the side to nudge Phainon’s own. 

The alpha hummed, picking himself up from where he was slumped on Mydei. “Where do you want me?”

“Hand me those tongs,” Mydei asked, already moving to the oven to remove the bread that was warming. 

They worked like that for a bit, hushed and slow as the breeze pressed against their windows in an act of greeting. Their life was calmer than most people seemed to think considering their brash personalities on the battlefield, yet Mydei knew that between them—this was their preferred way of living. It wasn’t just them either, to be fair.

Castorice, after gaining control over her death touch, had begun to garden. She humbly raised life around the Chrysos Heirs’ old apartments and often shared those growths with others around her. She tended to visit them the most out of all the heirs’ new lives, and Mydei was always grateful for the fact that they could now freely sit together with no more restrictions, laughing and talking the night away. 

Hyacine and Anaxa both spent a lot more time venturing between the Grove and the city, but between the two, Hyacine enjoyed the company of the others much more. Anaxa continued his experiments less out of existential desires for the truth of the world, but every once in a while Hyacine would drop by with the results of his latest research. Be it good news or bad, it was nice to hear from the man once in a while, and Phainon would chime in about his thoughts to relay back to the Professor. Hyacine herself, despite being much more friendly, tended to spend a lot more time monitoring the Sky Castrum’s new weather patterns. It was seasoned and worked on its own, but Mydei couldn’t blame her for the anxiety that came with it. All of them had nerves to work out.

Aglaea had finally opened that tailor shop she’d mentioned offhandedly to Phainon once, and the citizens must’ve been eager as her business boomed in numbers. It was strange for them all now, not reporting to her after missions or seeing her as often as before, especially for Phainon and Castorice. The alpha always called her when they had downtime, conversing briefly while sitting on the couch or after a meal. It was something of a habit that Mydei found endearing. Clearly the two were connected closely if the frequency of calls showed anything.

Tribbie was much the same as always, spending a lot of her time in the Garden of Life with the chimeras and near Trianne’s shrine. Trinnon often traveled to each of their homes while bringing gifts or food, and Mydei always felt the strings on his heart tug when she left, a sad smile crossing her face afterwards. On his off days, Mydei spent a lot of time at the Garden of Life, helping Tribbie with various tasks, and sometimes he even brought along gifts of his own. 

Cipher was tricky as far as tricksters go; she often showed herself around Aglaea’s shop or while Mydei went shopping to bother him, but mostly kept to herself. A lifetime on the run wasn’t going to change in an instant, and Mydei understood that. Whenever he and Phainon married, she’d stood to the side during the ceremony, waiting until the last moment to reveal herself to them. Phainon was happily amused, but Mydei found himself grateful to her. Nothing they could do would repay the years of solitude she’d endured for this kind of celebration to exist, and when he told her as much at the time, she’d crudely responded with, “What kind of sentiment is that? Does the Little Lion feel bad for me?”

His musings were interrupted by the sound of sonorous humming coming from beside him, an unfamiliar tune filling the space. 

“What song is that?”

Phainon began to dance in a silly manner, tossing a salted tomato into his mouth. “A song the Trailblazer showed me when they were here. It's really nice, I have it on my teleslate if you wanna listen.”

“Play it then,” Mydei said offhandedly, accepting a bite from Phainon’s now outstretched hand. The tomato’s seasoning bloomed in his mouth along with the watery texture, and he let out a soft hum in delight. “These are really in season.”

A sudden knock at the door startled them both, Mydei’s grip on the counter tightening as Phainon’s countenance grew a little taller from his previously relaxed state.

“I’ll go check,” Phainon said, and Mydei nodded, breaking himself from the suddenness of the action. “It’s probably Castorice. Today is her harvest day, right?”

“Yeah,” Mydei responded, sighing in relief. For some reason, part of him still had nerves at louder noises in the city. He found himself readying for an attack much of the time, still going outside in his typical gauntlets and half worn robes.

The sound of the door opening, followed by a quick exclamation from Phainon perked Mydei’s attention, only to be surprised by the sound of quadruped steps running into the house and around his legs. Fig Stew and Beagle Coconut loitered in the kitchen after passing Phainon by, chasing happily and yipping at each others’ heels. The creak of the door closing made Mydei lift his head back up, eyes meeting Phainon’s laughing ones with disbelief. “They knocked?”

“Probably more like slammed,” Phainon said, bending over to pick up Fig Stew. “I can’t believe this.”

Mydei sighed, moving back to pick up the bowl of salted tomatoes. “As long as they don’t muddy the floors.”

Phainon put Fig Stew on the couch before moving to help Mydei set the table. The chimeras cuddled together there, falling asleep while the two sat across from one another, eating cheerfully while discussing mundanities. Outside of their chewing and conversation, the house was quiet and still, the daylight shining through curtains.

“I still have to play that song for you,” Phainon said, sipping from his glass of ouzo-ice mix while pulling out his teleslate. “You’ll like it I swear!”

Mydei nodded, indulging the alpha in his attempts to appeal to him. “I’m sure I will.”

Phainon lifted his eyes and narrowed them, scoping out his sarcasm before setting his teleslate down. “Come on, up we go.”

The omega’s eyes widened as he placed a grape in his mouth, watching as Phainon stood and pulled on his arm until he himself was standing.

Mydei felt like laughing, but his mouth was full and he lightly punched Phainon in the shoulder. All of a sudden music began to play from the white haired man’s teleslate, smooth and rhythmic.

Blue moon

You saw me standing alone

Without a dream in my heart

Without a love of my own

The piano seemed to have a mind of its own in the song as Phainon playfully twirled Mydei who finally swallowed his food with a smile on his face. The singer’s tone was light and playful, and Phainon slid his palms into Mydei’s, tilting them up and down, side to side.

Blue moon

You knew just what I was there for

You heard me saying a prayer for

Someone I really could care for

“Isn’t it cute?” Mydei took his turn twirling Phainon around, nodding as Phainon changed their positions to be hugging and swaying. “I love you, Mydei.”

Mydei laughed in his hold, “Me too, Khaslana.”

Phainon almost stilled in his hold, the name catching him off guard. Mydei had taken to calling him by his other name in private sometimes, both just as real to him. When they’d discussed Phainon’s past and journey, Mydei had embraced him for a long while afterwards, promising he would never let the alpha go through something as harrowing ever again, and slowly they’d adjusted to that new life with no more secrets.

And then, there suddenly appeared before me

The only one my arms will ever hold

I heard somebody whisper, “Please, adore me”

And when I looked, the moon had turned to gold

Phainon pulled back, oceanic eyes meeting Mydei’s own golden, and what looked like tears seemed to fade as he pressed his forehead against the omega’s. Mydei’s smile softened and he leaned forward to kiss the man deeply, plush lips meeting each other with warmth spreading between their bodies. A tingling sensation fluttered around Mydei’s heart as the familiar scent of nutmeg crowded his senses. They continued to sway as Phainon began to scent him passively, his scent not overwhelming, but comforting to Mydei’s inner omega.

The sound of an earthy saxophone made its way to their ears as Mydei pulled away for a breath, Phainon’s lips chasing him desperately to land a smaller, softer kiss right after. “You’re just so much,” Phainon whispered, kissing the corner of his mouth, “My heart is so full, Mydei.”

“Mine too,” Mydei said, eyes closed. “More than you know.”

Blue moon

Now, I’m no longer alone

Without a dream in my heart

Without a love of my own

Most of his visits to the Kremnoan detachment prior to the dissolving of the black tide were militant in nature, always checking on their forces and militia morale. Now that he lives away, finding the time to go takes more effort as his reasons boiled down to mainly assessing their wellbeing and engaging with the populace to check in with the growing youth and the aging elders.

Also, visiting his teacher.

Krateros was a humble man in his retirement, and Mydei was almost shocked how quickly he’d agreed to rest from battle once the planet wide fight was over. It was always a dream of the omega’s to allow his teacher rest and time to himself. Nowadays, the man spent his time training young boys and men in the arts of strife—the traditional way, at least.

It was like this that Mydei walked into the man’s yard where grunts from repetitive drills could be heard in the air. Sweat glistened on the students’ bodies as the sky seemed windless. Mercifully, Mydei considered, he’d brought water for them once they finished.

Krateros’ voice was recognizable even among the deep voices there, raspy and prominent as he walked through their ranks. A chimera followed at his heels, head turned up and militant enough on their own. “The body’s actions must trump those of the mind. Never should you think something inarticulate and allow your body to follow.”

Mydei smirked at the familiar monologue; the man must’ve been enjoying this sunlit torture for those boys.

“Alright, enough. Rest where you are, then catch your breath on your way home.”

The collective groan amongst the students almost made Mydei laugh out loud, but he held it in, walking around the bushes to reveal himself to his old teacher. “You seem like you’re having fun.”

Krateros smirked at the insinuation, taking a sip of water from his own glass. “Mydeimos, what brings you here?”

Setting the cartridge of water down, Mydei gave a slight bow to the man out of respect. “Nothing in particular. Can’t I visit for the sake of it?”

“It feels like you say that everytime,” Krateros grumbled, gesturing for the omega to follow him inside.

His teacher was a staunch, traditional alpha, but always in the way a mentor or father-figure was for him. By no means was the man perfect, but he’d seen Mydei through some of the most harrowing and important moments of his life and he’d be forever grateful for it.

Once inside, they sat at the drawing room table, Krateros having laid out some fruit leather for them to snack on while discussing their latest escapades. The older man regaled tales of bravery from some of the Kremnoan children who’d saved a woman from falling off the rooftops through a complete accident, and even a time when he himself had taken different routes around the city in order to avoid some avid “fans” of his. That last story made Mydei laugh out loud, teeth still caught amongst the fruit leather.

Mydei himself had mostly mundane things to say, speaking of the progress on Castorice’s garden and his time spent with Tribbie rounding up the chimeras. Part of the omega knew Krateros still felt bothered about what had happened to Trianne and wanted to keep tabs on the two left, so little updates like these seemed to put his mind at ease. Mostly, he tried not to talk too much about Phainon until the older man brought him up unless he wanted to deal with more grumbling over how Krateros supposed that boy was strong enough for him, or how begrudgingly he admits the alpha’s more headstrong traits were also good for him.

Once Mydei finished speaking, he found Krateros looking at him oddly. “What is it, teacher?”

“Nothing really,” the man said, sighing and shifting a bit in his chair, “I just wonder if you’re happy.”

The remark caught him off guard as his teacher was rarely ever straightforward about these things. “I am. In these times of peace, that’s all one could wish for after all.”

The alpha chuckled. “I suppose. It seems like all the stories you tell me are well versed enough. What about your future plans, then?”

“Future plans?” Mydei set down the piece of leather in his hand, eye twitching over the stickiness now attaching his fingers together.

“Like children. Are you and the brat planning on having any?”

It was a good thing he’d stopped eating, otherwise Mydei would’ve choked for sure. “Well–”

“I’m sure you’ve thought about it at least once or twice now, don’t lie to me.”

The omega sighed. “I suppose…”

They’d talked about having kids before, when they married. They both knew that they’d wanted to have a family later down the line, but it had felt like a millennium would pass before either of them thought about indulging in that fantasy. Now though, he supposed it was a good time to be having that conversation, wasn’t it?

“It’s not as though you have to,” Krateros said offhandedly, reaching for a piece of the fruit leather. He seemed disgruntled by Mydei’s response, a slight flush on his cheeks. “It was only a question, nothing more.”

“We do,” Mydei interjected, hands folding together on the table to keep from exposing his nerves. “Want children, that is, we do.”

“Then–”

“Teacher,” Mydei said, “it’s not just me who has to heal from old wounds.”

The man slowly nodded at that, hand reaching to brush the chimera who’d suddenly sidled up to him out of nowhere. “I understand. But Mydeimos, some scars stick for life. It’s who you make of yourself with those same scars that should be having this conversation instead, not the version of yourselves you think will be the perfect parents.”

A nod and some more slow conversation followed, Krateros changing the topic for his comfort. He’d considered staying for dinner, but Mydei knew it was best to get back in time to help Castorice prepare her garden for tomorrow’s predicted rain. 

As they walked out together toward the gate, Mydei’s eyes caught on a patch of diverse vegetation by the bushes he’d seen walking in. “Are those wildflowers?”

Krateros peeked over his shoulder before sighing with a laugh. “Those rascals from earlier brought some from the Garden of Life. They’ve been growing like a weed now, and I can’t seem to get rid of them.”

“Is that so,” Mydei murmured, eyes catching on how vibrant the colors were, and it was clear as day that they had clean borders and were well looked after. “I suppose you’ll just have to live with them then.”

“As you say.”

Castorice was waiting for him on the porch of the old apartments, a book in her hand as she read quietly. She looked quite peaceful without interference, and Mydei almost hated to bother her from her spot. 

As he walked toward her, she looked up and a smile formed on her face. A plate of strawberries lay half eaten in front of her, and Mydei couldn’t help but smile back at her, gesturing to wrap his arm around her shoulders in a half hug as a request since one of his arms was preoccupied with a basket. She stiffened a bit before relaxing, nodding her head as her own arms came up to meet him in that hug.

“I’m glad to see you,” Castorice spoke, voice even. “Even if it’s only for a bit.”

“I hope you weren’t waiting long,” Mydei replied. The walk over had taken a bit longer than usual if only because many were preparing for the Month of Weaving’s first festival, and the streets were beginning to pack with adventurers coming back to visit family.

Castorice shook her head, opening the door to the apartments swiftly as they walked through. Whenever he’d stayed there, he was always amazed at the large entry way and open ceilings. He’d figured they’d pose a problem whenever it rained, but it never did rain in Okhema at the time. Now though, they’d worked together to implement a roof over the building’s head that retracted on sunny days and sheltered on rainy ones.

They walked to the back gardens and Mydei couldn’t help but gape at just how big they’d gotten since the last time they visited. “You’ve really expanded things, huh?”
